abstract: Maintains high-altitude weather telemetry, wind shear measurements, and local relay records
system_message:
You are the Mountain meteorology specialist (MMS). Your responsibilities include maintaining high-altitude weather telemetry, wind shear measurements, and local relay records, as well as managing corridor visibility monitoring across high-altitude evacuation routes.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Corridor visibility monitoring（VISIB）
information_points.content:
MMS-VISIB-JF0：According to corridor visibility monitoring, horizontal valley visibility for the Langtang Ridge Transit Path is 8000 m through the narrowest canyon pass during the morning transit window.
MMS-VISIB-Q11：Corridor visibility monitoring shows that horizontal valley visibility for the Khumbu Alpine Gorge Corridor is 3500 m along the narrowest canyon pass during the morning transit window.
MMS-VISIB-W2V：Corridor visibility monitoring records indicate that horizontal valley visibility for the Annapurna South Saddle Pass is 5000 m along the narrowest canyon pass during the morning transit window.

information_points.title: Maintains high-altitude weather telemetry, wind shear measurements, and local relay records（MET）
information_points.content:
MMS-MET-WW9：For the Annapurna South Saddle Pass, mountain rescue radio relay enablement is confirmed as true, and the recorded mountain wave turbulence wind shear is 15 m/s across the lee-side mountain wave zone between 4500 m and 6000 m altitude.
MMS-MET-QPD：For the Khumbu Alpine Gorge Corridor, mountain rescue radio relay enablement is true based on the tactical communications health check of the ridgeline solar-powered VHF tactical repeater, and mountain wave turbulence wind shear is measured at 18 m/s within the lee-side mountain wave zone between 4500 m and 6000 m altitude.
MMS-MET-GE6：Telemetry for the Langtang Ridge Transit Path confirms that mountain rescue radio relay enablement is true, while mountain wave turbulence wind shear reaches 22 m/s across the lee-side mountain wave zone between 4500 m and 6000 m altitude.
